title: Object/embed legacy context and safer alternatives
learningObjectives: Explain object/embed legacy context and safer alternatives and choose appropriate document or embedded-resource metadata.

understand.concept: object and embed can load external resources or plugin content and have historical uses for documents and media. Modern web pages usually prefer purpose-built elements such as img, video, audio, iframe, or links to downloadable files, depending on the content.
understand.whyItMatters: Legacy embedding can have inconsistent behaviour and security implications. Choose a modern element that matches the resource and provide a fallback or direct link when appropriate.
understand.analogy: Older embed mechanisms are general-purpose adapters; modern HTML offers specialised elements for common resource types.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; metadata and embedding behaviour follow browser, HTTP, and search-engine processing rules.

explain.narrative: The example uses a direct link for a document and the native video element with fallback content for media.

examples.explanation: The example uses a direct link for a document and the native video element with fallback content for media.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered or document-head example demonstrating the HTML feature.

practise.guidedTask: For a PDF, video, image, and external interactive site, choose an appropriate modern HTML element and explain the fallback.
practise.independentTask: Prepare a document head or embed example. Check accessibility, security permissions, and whether metadata accurately describes the content.
hints: Use absolute canonical URLs when declaring a canonical target.
Never treat crawler directives as access control.
Use restrictive iframe permissions and a meaningful title.

questions.prompt: Which element is purpose-built for embedding video media?
questions.explanation: The video element is the native HTML element for video content.

questions.prompt: Which principle should guide metadata and embedding?
options: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
Use metadata as a substitute for authentication
Grant every embedded document all permissions
questions.answer: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate and embedded resources should receive only necessary capabilities.
